choice.combine: Central nervous system with sensory routes

expectation: The motor axons should connect the central nervous system to peripheral routes.

effect: The motor routes completed the nervous system model. The result shows sensory and motor signals travelling on different axons in the same spinal nerve, then using separate roots at the cord.
reaction: Seeing where the two routes separate helped make their connection clearer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the sensory and motor routes was most worthwhile: the pictures showed where the sensory cell bodies stay and how incoming and outgoing signals relate to the spinal cord.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building four central regions in much the same way became a little repetitive, although their insets gave them different jobs.

surprise.text: I expected to connect the cerebellum directly to the brainstem, but the game required the cerebrum connection first and made it automatically.

arbitrary.text: That required order felt somewhat arbitrary: the earlier picture showed cerebellar connecting bundles, but did not explain why the cerebrum had to be attached first.

continue.text: I would choose to continue to see how the nerve branches connect to tissues, especially the arm muscles. The finished model leaves those connections visibly open.
